text:
lee: Heads up — our tenant-throttle detector just fired for tenant=atlas in eu-west-1. Seeing repeated per-GPU throttle events + tail-latency spikes over the last 10m. Proposing a graded fallback routing (burst lane -> dedicated-fallback -> concurrency cap). Thoughts? cc @vikram @maria

maria: Can you paste the short query and any correlation with egress/nvlink errors? Also did this align with any recent deploys?

lee: quick query I ran in metrics (5m window):
```
sum(rate(gpu_token_latency_seconds_bucket{tenant=\"atlas\"}[5m])) by (le)
```
Spikes line up with a sustained KV cache miss rate increase. No infra deploys at the time.

aj: Agree with graded fallbacks. My suggested config prototype:
```
fallbacks:
  - name: burst_pool_shallow
    type: burst_pool
    max_duration_sec: 60
    cost_cap_per_request: 0.02
  - name: dedicated_fallback_lowprio
    type: dedicated_pool
    priority: low
    max_replica: 2
  - name: concurrency_soft_cap
    type: tenant_rate_limit
    qps: 1.5 * baseline
```
Keep it conservative for the first rollout.

ops-bot: Patch applied to routing service: add support for "cost_cap_per_request" on burst_pool. CI: ✅, canary deploy scheduled.

vikram: Cost-note: burst pool is billed at dedicated rates. We need a safety gate so we don't auto-burn credits for non-SLA traffic. Suggest a route condition: only for tenants with sla_tier >= gold or when error_rate>0.5%.

maria: Also add a fallback_count metric so we can alert on repeated fallbacks — that will help with billing/backfill tickets. Dashboard quick link: https://dash.redwood.tools/d/atlas/tenant-fallbacks (will add panels)

sre-oncall: If we route to dedicated_fallback_lowprio we need preemption handling. Add a short lived MV cache checkpoint so model warmup doesn't spike tail. Otherwise we might see 5-10s cold starts on failover.

zach: Another failure mode: if multiple tenants hit fallback simultaneously we may saturate the burst pool. We should have a token-bucket limiter per-az and a global throttle back to shared queues.

lee: Good catches. Proposed rollout plan:
- 1) Add fallback_count metric + dashboard (maria)
- 2) Canary config for atlas in eu-west-1 for 2 hours with cost_cap_per_request=0.015 and sla gate=gold (lee/aj)
- 3) Add preemption-safe warmup checkpoint in agent (sre-oncall)
- 4) Global AZ limiter + overflow to shared queue (zach)

aj: I can open the PR for the routing config and add a dry-run mode that only emits fallback_count but doesn't actually route. We should run dry-run for 30m before enabling.

maria: I'll add dashboard panels and an alert: fallback_count_rate > 5/min over 10m -> paged to eng-infra (severity=low).

vikram: What about tenant-controlled opt-out? Some customers won't want automatic fallback. Add a tenant flag: allow_fallbacks = true by default. We'll respect the tenant setting.

lee: Sounds good. Action owners: aj(PR + dry-run), maria(dash & alert), sre-oncall(warmup checkpoint), zach(az limiter). I'll schedule the canary for tomorrow 09:00 UTC and post results here. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: routing-config-v2 -> eu-west-1 (atlas) at 2025-06-12T09:00:00Z.

lee: Thanks — will follow up with post-canary summary.

maria: :rocket:

sre-oncall: Quick note — add a short TTL to KV checkpoint (30s) so we don't hold memory long during mass failovers.

lee: noted.

zach: Also adding a manual emergency cutoff flag for ops if costs spike: /ops fallback-shutdown <az>

lee: Perfect. I'll include that in the runbook.

(Reaction thread: many :white_check_mark: and :eyes:)
